questions.stem: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856 owed its passage largely to whose sustained petition campaign submitted to the British administration?

options.option_text: Raja Ram Mohan Roy, who campaigned against Sati in Bengal
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who submitted petitions to the British
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, who championed Hindu revivalism in Maharashtra
Keshab Chandra Sen, who led the progressive wing of Brahmo Samaj

questions.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar gathered thousands of signatures and submitted two major petitions to the colonial legislature, directly driving passage of the Act in 1856. Ram Mohan Roy's campaign targeted Sati, leading to its abolition in 1829 — a separate evil addressed two decades earlier. Tilak was a political revivalist, not a widow-remarriage advocate.

questions.stem: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 with which stated primary aim?

options.option_text: Child marriage practices prevalent among upper-caste Hindu families
Brahminical priesthood's monopoly over religious and social rituals
The purdah system restricting women's movement in western India
Restrictions on widow remarriage imposed by orthodox Hindu society

questions.explanation: Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth-Seekers' Society) was founded to liberate Shudras and Ati-Shudras from Brahminical intermediaries, enabling direct access to God without priestly sanction. Widow remarriage was Vidyasagar's central cause; the purdah critique belonged primarily to reformers in Bengal and northern India, not Phule's movement.

questions.stem: The periodical 'Tattvabodhini Patrika', launched in 1843 to spread rational religion and oppose idol worship, was the official organ of which body?

options.option_text: Prarthana Samaj, the reform society founded in Bombay in 1867
Tattvabodhini Sabha, founded by Debendranath Tagore in Bengal
Arya Samaj, established by Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay in 1875
Young Bengal Movement, led by Henry Vivian Derozio in Calcutta

questions.explanation: Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839; its journal launched in 1843 propagated Brahmo monotheism and became a vehicle for Bengali rational thought. Arya Samaj's mouthpiece was 'Arya Patrika'. The Young Bengal Movement collapsed by the 1830s — over a decade before this journal appeared — making it chronologically impossible.

questions.stem: The Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay in 1867 primarily under the inspiration of which visiting reformer or organisation from Bengal?

options.option_text: Paramahansa Mandali's rationalist tradition in western India
Brahmo Samaj, after Keshab Chandra Sen's inspirational Bombay visit
Adi Brahmo Samaj under Debendranath Tagore's conservative leadership
Theosophical Society's syncretist philosophy introduced in Bombay

questions.explanation: Keshab Chandra Sen's 1864 visit to Bombay inspired Atmaram Pandurang and others to found the Prarthana Samaj in 1867 on Brahmo Samaj lines. Option C is a trap: Debendranath's Adi Brahmo Samaj was the conservative faction that resisted Keshab's reforms — the opposite spirit to what inspired Prarthana. The Theosophical Society arrived in India only in 1879, a full decade later.

questions.stem: The Ramakrishna Mission, founded in 1897, established its permanent headquarters at which site distinct from where Ramakrishna Paramahamsa himself lived and worshipped?

options.option_text: Dakshineswar Kali Temple, where Ramakrishna served as a priest
Belur Math, on the western bank of the Hooghly river near Kolkata
Baranagar Math, the earliest monastery set up after Ramakrishna's passing
Kamarpukur village, the birthplace of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa

questions.explanation: Belur Math, consecrated by Vivekananda in 1898–1899 on the western bank of the Hooghly, became the Mission's registered headquarters. Dakshineswar (eastern bank) is where Ramakrishna worshipped under Rani Rashmoni's patronage — a frequent wrong answer. Baranagar Math was only a temporary shelter for disciples set up in 1886 before the Mission was formally organised.

questions.stem: The Paramahansa Mandali, a clandestine reform circle in mid-19th century Maharashtra, challenged caste hierarchy through which specific transgressive practice at its secret meetings?

options.option_text: Publicly burning copies of Manusmriti at reformist gatherings
Holding inter-dining sessions with food cooked by lower-caste members
Conducting inter-caste marriages without any Brahmin ritual sanction
Organising public widow remarriage ceremonies before British officials

questions.explanation: Founded c.1849 by Dadoba Pandurang Tarkhadkar, the Mandali held secret gatherings where members shared food prepared by non-Brahmin individuals, violating the ritual food-purity rules at the heart of caste exclusion. Option A is the most tempting distractor but is wrong: burning Manusmriti is associated with B.R. Ambedkar at Mahad in 1927. Inter-caste marriages were championed by Phule and Agarkar, not this body.

questions.stem: The 'Rehnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha', co-founded by Dadabhai Naoroji in Bombay in 1851, was a modernising reform association within which religious community?

options.option_text: Bengali Muslim community seeking Western education under British patronage
Parsi (Zoroastrian) community of western India seeking liturgical reform
Sikh community of Punjab resisting Brahmo Samaj's influence in 1860s
Cochin Jewish community seeking integration with broader Hindu society

questions.explanation: Rehnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (Religious Reform Association of Zoroastrianism) was founded in 1851 by Dadabhai Naoroji, Naoroji Furdonji, and S.S. Bengali to reform Parsi practices, introduce intelligible prayers, and tackle child marriage within the community. Option A is the chief distractor: the Bengali Muslim reform body was Nawab Abdul Latif's Mohammedan Literary Society (1863), a different community, a different city, and a different decade.
